Header: Xanthomonas campestris pv. musacearum Banana Xanthomonas Wilt

Prevention: Use healthy planting materials (suckers and corms) from disease-free areas.
Or, get clean banana suckers produced under tissue-culture from trusted sources like
Remove the male flower bud using a forked stick (not a knife) after the last hand has formed, to reduce the risk of the banana plant being diseased through the male flower.
Once the disease has been detected, always disinfect tools like hoes, machetes and knives during and after use, to avoid spreading the bacteria to healthy plants.
Sterilise tools by flaming until hot or with bleach.
Follow national quarantine procedures, particularly do not transport bananas out of infected areas.
Xanthomonas wilt is a bacterial disease spread by wasps feeding on nectar in infected male banana flowers and then on healthy flowers.
The disease is also spread through contaminated cutting tools.
Monitoring: Check plantation for symptoms once a week in first 6 months of planting, and later once per month.
Look for wilting in flowers, yellowing of young and old leaves which soon turn brown.
Purple leaves of bract (banana flower) become black and shrivelled before they die.
When cut open, the banana fruit has dark stains including those that are green.
Cut a cross section of stem and observe oozing of a creamy to pale yellow fluid to confirm bacterial disease.
Fungal wilt diseases do not ooze.
Xanthomonas wilt can be confused with a fungal disease, Panama disease (Fusarium wilt).
Fusarium banana, yellowing and wilting of leaves progresses from older to younger leaves; wilted leaves may snap at the base and hang down the stem.
Xanthomonas , wilting begins with any leaf and the infected leaves snap along the leaf blade.
Direct Control: Remove diseased plants and dispose carefully by burying or burning them 1m deep and 100m away from banana plantations.
Single stem removal will help minimise infection of new plants but this will not eliminate the disease.
Remove infected plants as soon as they are noticed when up to 5-15% of the banana plantation is diseased.
Restrictions: There are no recommended chemicals to control
Once the plant is infected there is no treatment to cure it from the disease.
